text: Using the properties of determinants, prove that $\begin{vmatrix}1 & a & a^2 \\ 1 & b & b^2 \\ 1 & c & c^2\end{vmatrix} = (a - b)(b - c)(c - a)$.

points.text: Apply $R_1 \to R_1 - R_2$ and $R_2 \to R_2 - R_3$, so the first column becomes $0, 0, 1$.
Take out the common factors $(a - b)$ and $(b - c)$ from the first two rows.
Expanding along the first column leaves $(a - b)(b - c)\begin{vmatrix}1 & a + b \\ 1 & b + c\end{vmatrix}$.
This 2 by 2 determinant is $b + c - a - b = c - a$, which gives the result.
